title: Time Investigation: ICE Detention Deaths at 22-Year High; Agency Simultaneously Reduced Public Death Reporting
excerpt: A Time investigation found that more than 30 people had died in ICE detention since October 2025 and that deaths through mid-2026 were running at a 22-year high—while ICE simultaneously reduced the information it publishes about individual deaths and eliminated requirements to report post-release deaths.
content:
A Time magazine investigation published on August 10, 2026 documented that more than 30 people had died in ICE detention since October 2025, with the current fiscal year's death rate reaching a 22-year high according to the JAMA research letter published in April.

Simultaneously, ICE reduced the information it makes public about detainee deaths. In June 2026, the agency announced it would stop reporting instances when people die soon after being released from custody—eliminating an accountability mechanism put in place by the Biden administration in 2021.

  • Between October and January 19, 2026 alone—the window analyzed in the JAMA study—18 immigration detainee deaths were reported; at least 17 more people died while held by ICE in subsequent months.
  • By comparison, only 3 people died in ICE detention during the full FY2022.
  • DHS maintained in a statement to TIME that "there has been NO spike in deaths," citing aggregate detention population statistics, while independent researchers documented a mortality rate nearly seven times the FY2023 level.
  • Researchers identified causes of death as "identifiable and amenable to intervention" — including cardiovascular disease, suicide, and infectious disease — categories routinely treated in community medicine.
"There isn't a tradition in this country of treating deaths in custody seriously enough to make sure that we understand what went wrong." — Sharon Dolovich, UCLA Law professor
